expectation: Cytoplasmic stain in a minority of cells: macrophages, microglia, monocytes and dendritic cells. They should be ramified or irregular cells scattered singly or in clusters in stroma and lamina propria, with epithelium unstained.
observed: A shows yellow signal concentrated in the lamina propria cores of villus-like folds, with epithelium and lumen dark. B has bright branched yellow cells at the stromal edge, and C is nearly empty. D shows irregular, process-bearing cells. E1 shows many bright branched cells that partly overlap CD163 in E3.
why: Bright, branched cytoplasmic cells sit in the stromal cores, avoid the epithelium, and partly overlap CD163 as a subset relation predicts.
notes: Yellow cells are macrophage-shaped and confined to stroma and villus cores; epithelium and empty areas stay dark. Many IBA1 cells lie on or beside CD163 cells, and IBA1-only cells are consistent with the subset relation.
